_comment: Room names for one building, used by the patrol agent.
THE SOURCE OF TRUTH IS THE WEB CONSOLE'S LABELS TABLE. A user types what
they read on the floor plan, so this file mirrors `web/드론 관제.dc.html`
(LABELS, ~line 542) — the same table lives in `web/HAUNTED OPS.dc.html`.
The console never asks the server for names (nothing calls GET /api/rooms,
and /api/intent's `names` field is ignored), so the two tables are kept in
sync BY HAND. If a label changes over there, change it here too or that
room stops being reachable by voice/text.
The earlier person-nicknames (현우방 -> 002_012, 규철방 -> 002_014) are gone
on purpose: they collided with the labels, which put a DIFFERENT person on
those rooms (012 reads 채원…, 014 reads 현우…). Typing what the screen said
flew the drone somewhere else. One naming system now, the one on screen.
Per room: the full label first (it becomes RoomInfo.display), then the
shorter forms a person actually types. Matching is plain substring against
the user's text, longest alias first, so keep them distinctive — a bare
'실' or '방' would match half the building. Parenthesised labels also get a
paren-free form, because the alias has to appear IN what the user typed.
'복도' is deliberately shared by 001_010 / 002_011 / 002_023: it reads as a
kind of room ('복도 순찰해줘' -> every corridor), and naming a floor narrows
it back down ('2층 복도' -> 001_010) via the floor filter in resolve_rooms.
Keys are room_name (the <floor>_<room> dir suffix). Aliases are injected
into the LLM room directory AND matched by substring when the LLM misses.
floor_offset: floor index 0 is displayed as this 층 number (1 = 0 -> '1층').
